title: Staying Put When Things Fall Apart
overview: When someone urges the singer to run from danger, he answers that he trusts the LORD, who sees everyone clearly and will judge fairly.

parts.label: Advice to run away (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: Someone tells the singer to fly like a bird to the hills, because enemies are aiming at him from the dark and the 'foundations' of society, its law and order, are crumbling. It is unclear whether these are worried friends or mocking enemies, but the singer refuses because he has already made the LORD his shelter.

parts.label: The LORD watches from his throne (vv. 4-5)
parts.note: The temple here most likely means God's home in heaven, where he rules and looks closely at every person, the way a metalworker tests metal to learn its true worth. He tests good people, but those who love violence he hates, and the psalm says so plainly.

parts.label: Judgment on the violent (v. 6)
parts.note: Fiery coals, burning sulfur and a scorching wind echo the story of Sodom and Gomorrah's destruction. These are vivid pictures of sudden and complete ruin for those who love violence.

parts.label: A final hope (v. 7)
parts.note: The psalm ends by saying the LORD loves what is just and the upright will 'see his face.' This is usually understood to mean they will know God's favor and closeness, though exactly what the singer pictured is not spelled out.

think: When the world around you seems to be coming apart, what helps you decide whether to stand your ground or get out?
